---
title: "Outlier detection with PCA scores"
description: >-
  Score plot with Hotelling's ellipses, T-squared control chart, and the contribution of
  each component to the flagged samples.
---

This example fits a PCA model to the wine data and looks for unusual samples among the
samples the model was fitted on. All the numbers in the text are computed when this
page is built.

## Data and PCA model

The wine data has 178 samples and 13 chemical measurements. The measurements are
standardized, since they have different units, and all principal components are kept.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
from sklearn.datasets import load_wine
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from pyEllipse import hotelling_coordinates, hotelling_parameters

X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(load_wine().data)
pca = PCA().fit(X)
scores = pca.transform(X)
explained = pca.explained_variance_ratio_

pd.DataFrame(
    {"Explained variance": explained, "Cumulative": np.cumsum(explained)},
    index=[f"PC{j}" for j in range(1, len(explained) + 1)],
).head(6).style.format("{:.1%}")
```

```{python}
#| include: false
plt.style.use("../_pyellipse.mplstyle")
BLUE, ORANGE, INK, MUTED = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#373a3c", "#6c757d"
# Sequential blue ramp, light to dark (validated for ordered steps on white)
T2_CMAP = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "t2", ["#86b6ef", "#5598e7", "#2a78d6", "#1c5cab", "#104281"]
)
```

The scores are the samples the model was fitted on, so the exact limit of T-squared for
them is the Beta limit, `method="beta"` (see [Control limits](../theory.qmd#sec-limits)).

## Score plot with Hotelling's ellipses

`hotelling_parameters` computes T-squared on the first two components and its cutoffs,
and `hotelling_coordinates` the points of the matching ellipses.

```{python}
res_2 = hotelling_parameters(scores, pcx=1, pcy=2, method="beta")
ellipse_95 = hotelling_coordinates(scores, pcx=1, pcy=2, conf_limit=0.95, method="beta")
ellipse_99 = hotelling_coordinates(scores, pcx=1, pcy=2, conf_limit=0.99, method="beta")

t2_2 = res_2["Tsquared"]["value"]
above_95 = np.flatnonzero(t2_2 > res_2["cutoff_95pct"])
res_2["Ellipse"].round(3)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-scores
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Scores on the first two principal components, coloured by their T-squared value on
#|   these components, with the 95% and 99% Hotelling's ellipses (Beta limits).
#| code-fold: true
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
for ellipse, label, width in [(ellipse_95, "95%", 1), (ellipse_99, "99%", 1.5)]:
    ax.plot(ellipse["x"], ellipse["y"], color=INK, lw=width)
    top = ellipse["y"].idxmax()
    ax.annotate(label, (ellipse["x"][top], ellipse["y"][top]), xytext=(0, 4),
                textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK)
points = ax.scatter(scores[:, 0], scores[:, 1], c=t2_2, cmap=T2_CMAP, s=36,
                    edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8, zorder=3)
fig.colorbar(points, ax=ax, label="T² on PC1 and PC2", shrink=0.8)
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.set_xlabel(f"PC1 ({explained[0]:.1%})")
ax.set_ylabel(f"PC2 ({explained[1]:.1%})")
plt.show()
```

The scores are uncorrelated, so the ellipses are aligned with the axes (`angle` is 0).
On these two components, `{python} len(above_95)` samples lie outside the 95% ellipse
(rows `{python} ", ".join(map(str, above_95))`), and none outside the 99% ellipse.

## T-squared on more components

Two components explain only `{python} f"{explained[:2].sum():.0%}"` of the variance.
With `threshold=0.8`, `hotelling_parameters` uses the smallest number of components that
explain at least 80% of it.

```{python}
res = hotelling_parameters(scores, threshold=0.8, method="beta")
k = res["nb_comp"]
t2 = res["Tsquared"]["value"]
flagged = np.flatnonzero(t2 > res["cutoff_99pct"])
print(f"{k} components, 95% limit {res['cutoff_95pct']:.2f}, 99% limit {res['cutoff_99pct']:.2f}")
print("Rows above the 99% limit:", flagged.tolist())
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-control-chart
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   T-squared of each sample on the components that explain 80% of the variance, with
#|   the 95% and 99% Beta limits. The samples above the 99% limit are labelled with their row number.
#| code-fold: true
rows = np.arange(len(t2))
above = t2.to_numpy() > res["cutoff_99pct"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
for level, width in [("95", 1), ("99", 1.5)]:
    cutoff = res[f"cutoff_{level}pct"]
    ax.axhline(cutoff, color=INK if level == "99" else MUTED, lw=width)
    ax.annotate(f"{level}% limit", (1, cutoff), xycoords=("axes fraction", "data"),
                xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", va="bottom",
                color=INK)
ax.scatter(rows[~above], t2[~above], s=24, color=BLUE, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8,
           label="Below the 99% limit", zorder=3)
ax.scatter(rows[above], t2[above], s=36, color=ORANGE, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8,
           label="Above the 99% limit", zorder=3)
for row in rows[above]:
    ax.annotate(str(row), (row, t2[row]), xytext=(0, 6), textcoords="offset points",
                ha="center", fontsize=9, color=INK)
ax.set_xlim(-2, len(t2) + 1)
ax.set_xlabel("Sample (row number)")
ax.set_ylabel(f"T² on {k} components")
ax.legend(loc="upper left")
plt.show()
```

## Which components make a sample unusual?

For uncorrelated scores, T-squared is a sum of one term per component,
$t_{ij}^2 / s_j^2$ (see [Uncorrelated scores](../theory.qmd#uncorrelated-scores)). These
contributions show which components make each flagged sample unusual; their sum is the
T-squared value returned by `hotelling_parameters`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-contributions
#| tbl-cap: "Contribution of each component to the T-squared value of the samples above the 99% limit. The largest contribution of each sample is in bold."
components = [f"PC{j}" for j in range(1, k + 1)]
contributions = pd.DataFrame(
    scores[:, :k] ** 2 / scores[:, :k].var(axis=0, ddof=1), columns=components
)
assert np.allclose(contributions.sum(axis=1), t2)  # the contributions add up to T-squared

table = contributions.loc[flagged].assign(**{"T²": t2[flagged]})
table.index.name = "Row"
(
    table.style.format("{:.2f}")
    .highlight_max(axis=1, subset=components, props="font-weight: bold")
)
```

## F or Beta limit?

The default `method="f"` gives larger limits than `method="beta"`; for the samples the
model was fitted on, it is conservative, so it can miss samples that the exact Beta
limit flags.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-methods
#| tbl-cap: "Limits of T-squared on the components that explain 80% of the variance, and number of samples above them, by method and confidence level."
summary = []
for method in ["beta", "f"]:
    r = hotelling_parameters(scores, threshold=0.8, method=method)
    for level in ["95", "99"]:
        cutoff = r[f"cutoff_{level}pct"]
        summary.append({"Method": method, "Level": f"{level}%", "Limit": cutoff,
                        "Samples above": int((r["Tsquared"]["value"] > cutoff).sum())})
pd.DataFrame(summary).style.hide(axis="index").format({"Limit": "{:.2f}"})
```

With `{python} len(t2)` samples, the two limits are close; for small data sets, the
difference is much larger (see the [figure of the limits](../theory.qmd#fig-limits) on
the Theory page).
